answer: Unique-Hardware Attestation Ledger. Each identity must present a device key fused into silicon at manufacture, signed by the foundry over a public ledger; the registry rejects any key seen before, so one physical chip yields one identity. A reef of recycled keys cannot form because collisions are detected at registration. Operators face a hollow return: faking N identities requires N distinct fabricated dies, each costing wafer and packaging. Residual ivory from resold devices is voided when the owner revokes, so theft gains nothing.
